div.head: Iudex 3
div.ab: Iudicia debent esse sine omni haderunga, cur non parcatur alicui diuiti uel egeno, amico uel inimico ius publicum recitari.
Domas sceolon beon butan ælcere hadarunge: þæt ys, þæt he ne murne naðer ne rycum ne heanum, ne leofum ne laðum folcriht to recceanne.
Urtheilssprüche sollen ohne jede Personen-Rücksicht sein: d. h. dass er sich nicht scheue, weder Reichen [Grossen] noch Niederen, nicht Lieben noch Verhassten Gemeinrecht zuzuerkennen.
Judgments must be without any respect of persons: that is, that he not shrink from awarding common law to rich [great] or lowly, to friend or foe.

Judgements are to be made without regard for the individual: that is, he [the judge] is not to care whether [the accused] is rich or poor, a friend or enemy – full legal rights are to be extended [to all].
